messages:
Rina: Heads-up 1: support reported confusion: customers see 429/503 but we surface the same console badge 'throttled'. They can't tell whether it was a tenant quota event, global capacity, or a model problem. We need a clearer provenance surface.
Diego: +1. Suggest we stop overloading a single `error_code` and add an explicit `error_category` string field clients can rely on: e.g. `transient_capacity`, `tenant_throttle`, `model_fault`, `model_degraded`. Keep HTTP semantics (429 vs 5xx) but make `error_category` stable.
Priya: For responses I prefer a header `x-rw-error-provenance` (routing|tenant|model|fallback) and a JSON field `error_category` in the response body. Headers are easier for observability but some CDNs/proxies strip custom headers.
Noel: Good point about proxies. For public API responses we should include the advisory JSON field because bodies are preserved. Header as quick signal, body as canonical. We must avoid exposing tenant IDs or sensitive metadata in either place.
Rina: UX/copy: console should show a short human label + one-line action. Suggestions: "Capacity pressure 1: try again in a minute" (for transient_capacity), "Tenant quota reached 1: contact billing" (for tenant_throttle), "Model error 1: using fallback" (for model_fault/degraded). We'll link to runbook snippets.
Diego: Telemetry plan: emit counter `errors.provenance` with tag `provenance=<routing|tenant|model|fallback>` at 100%. Additionally sample detailed spans (~0.5% of events) with trace context and prompt hash for debugging quality regressions. Keep sampled traces in secure store.
Priya: Also add a boolean `retryable` in the JSON so SDKs can make decisions. Map: transient_capacity -> retryable=true, model_degraded -> retryable=false (but surface fallback_applied=true). Tenant_throttle -> retryable=false and include `retry_after` when available.
Noel: SDK API idea: add `ErrorProvenance` enum + helper `shouldRetry()` that inspects `error_category` and `retry_after`. Also log a one-line human reason for telemetry.
Rina: Security: ensure headers never contain tenant identifiers. If we must include tenant context for support, it goes to telemetry only, not to response headers or body.
Diego: Edge case: what if we route to a fallback and the fallback returns 200 but with low-quality indicators? We should still mark request `quality.signal=degraded` in telemetry and add response body field `fallback_applied:true` + `fallback_reason:"model_latency|quota_fallback"`. Console can surface a yellow badge.
Priya: Rollout: feature-flag the new fields on platform for internal clients first, 72h metrics, then enable for hosted clusters. After 2 weeks if metrics look stable ship SDK helpers in patch releases. Deprecate old `INTERNAL` opaque mapping in 90 days with notices.
Noel: Tests needed: integration test through edge proxies to ensure headers survive, contract tests for SDKs, and e2e with console badge toggles. Also add a dataplane linter that fails if we accidentally include tenant_id in responses.
Rina: Can we add a minimal example response snippet for docs? e.g. { "status":429, "error":"Too Many Requests", "error_category":"tenant_throttle", "retry_after":"3600", "action":"contact-billing" } We'll put that in the API changelog.
Diego: I'll add instrumentation mappings and the kql/metrics queries for dashboards (split by provenance, p95 latency, error-rate trend). We'll make an alert on >5% of requests being `model_fault` for a route.
Priya: Console designers: Use succinct verb-first copy. Example badges: "Capacity pressure 1: Retry" (green), "Tenant quota 1: Contact" (red), "Model fallback 1: Quality alert" (yellow). Also add hover tooltip with runbook link.
Noel: Deploy-bot can do a staged canary once infra merges: please include a canary flag so we can run on a small subset of tenants.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy triggered: `feature/error-provenance` -> group eng-plat-canary. Build 10214. See /deploys/10214 :rocket:
Rina: Last operational note: we should ensure observability pipelines index the new `error_category` string as a keyword to avoid high-cardinality issues. Diego, can you add that to the RFC?
Diego: Will do. Also I'll include a privacy section noting sampled traces retention and access controls.
Priya: I'll draft SDK PR and a short migration guide for customers.
Noel: I'll prepare the console mockups and copy.
Rina: Great. I'll write a short RFC and ping security + support. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
